scams.name: Tram Pickpocketing
scams.description: Montpellier's tram system is a prime hunting ground for organized pickpocket teams. Thieves work in groups during busy periods, especially during boarding and exiting when passengers are distracted and pressed together. One person creates a distraction or blocks movement while accomplices slip hands into bags and pockets.
scams.avoidance: Wear bags zipped and close to your body in front. Keep hands on your belongings during boarding and exiting. Avoid placing phones or wallets in back pockets. Stay alert at busy stops like Comedie and Gare Saint-Roch.
scams.location: Tram Line 1 & 2, Gare Saint-Roch tram stop, Comedie tram stop

scams.name: Place de la Comedie Pickpocketing
scams.description: Place de la Comedie, Montpellier's grand central square, attracts tourists and thieves alike. Pickpockets blend into the crowds around the iconic Three Graces fountain, targeting distracted visitors taking photos or sitting at outdoor cafes. Teams work together - one distracts by asking for directions while another steals valuables.
scams.avoidance: Keep bags on your lap or looped around chair legs at cafes. Be wary of anyone approaching with distractions. Don't leave phones or wallets on cafe tables. Stay alert while taking photos.
scams.location: Place de la Comedie, Three Graces Fountain area, Opera Comedie entrance

scams.name: Gare Saint-Roch Train Station Theft
scams.description: Montpellier's main train station is a hotspot for opportunistic theft targeting travelers burdened with luggage. Thieves observe arriving tourists who appear lost or confused, then strike when victims are distracted checking schedules, buying tickets, or managing bags. At night, the station vicinity has a rougher reputation.
scams.avoidance: Keep luggage close and in sight at all times. Don't appear lost - research your route before arriving. Be extra vigilant during boarding and at station stops. Avoid lingering in the station area at night.
scams.location: Montpellier Saint-Roch train station, platforms, tram stop outside station

scams.name: TGV Train Luggage Theft
scams.description: Thieves board TGV trains during brief station stops, posing as passengers. They position themselves with views of the luggage racks and wait for any distraction. Working in teams, one person engages the victim in conversation while the other grabs luggage from the rack and exits just before the doors close. Up to 400 such incidents occur monthly on French trains.
scams.avoidance: Keep valuables and essentials in a small bag you keep with you. Use cable locks to secure luggage to racks. Sit where you can see your luggage. Stay alert during station stops.
scams.location: TGV trains to/from Montpellier, luggage racks, during station stops

scams.name: Fake Petition / Deaf Charity Scam
scams.description: Scammers approach tourists with clipboards, often pretending to be deaf-mute and collecting signatures for a fake charity. The petition is typically written in English to target foreign visitors. While you're distracted reading or signing, accomplices pickpocket you. If you sign, they demand a donation and can become aggressive when refused.
scams.avoidance: Firmly say 'Non merci' and keep walking without slowing down. Never sign anything on the street. Don't engage in conversation. Keep hands on your belongings when approached.
scams.location: Place de la Comedie, Esplanade de l'Europe, tourist attractions

scams.name: Gold Ring Scam
scams.description: A stranger bends down near you and picks up what appears to be a gold ring, asking if you dropped it. When you say no, they examine it and claim it's marked '18k gold' and must be valuable. They offer to sell it or guilt you into giving them a 'finder's fee.' The ring is worthless brass, and while you're engaged, an accomplice may be pickpocketing you.
scams.avoidance: Simply say 'no' and walk away without engaging. Don't examine or touch the ring. Keep moving and maintain awareness of your surroundings.
scams.location: Place de la Comedie, Esplanade Charles de Gaulle, pedestrian streets in Ecusson

scams.name: Taxi Overcharging / Broken Meter Scam
scams.description: Some taxi drivers target tourists by claiming the meter is broken and quoting inflated flat rates, taking unnecessarily long routes, or failing to reset the meter to the base fare before starting. The airport to city center trip should cost approximately 35 euros during the day and 42 euros at night, but tourists may pay significantly more.
scams.avoidance: Know approximate fares before traveling (airport to center: ~35 euros day, ~42 euros night). Insist on using the meter and verify it starts at 2 euros. Track your route on Google Maps. Use official taxi stands or ride-hailing apps.
scams.location: Montpellier-Mediterranee Airport, Gare Saint-Roch train station, tourist areas

scams.name: Tram Ticket Enforcement Trap
scams.description: Montpellier enforces strict ticket validation rules. Tourists who purchase valid tickets but don't validate them immediately upon boarding face fines. Officers have been reported to use intimidating tactics. Unlike other French cities, Montpellier's system requires immediate validation.
scams.avoidance: Always validate your ticket immediately upon boarding - before finding a seat. Keep validated tickets until you exit the tram. Consider using contactless payment cards which auto-validate. Purchase tickets via the TAM app.
scams.location: All tram lines, particularly busy tram stops

scams.name: Restaurant Bill Padding
scams.description: Some restaurants in tourist areas inflate bills with hidden charges or serve items not ordered. Common tactics include automatically bringing expensive bottled water instead of offering free tap water, adding cover charges not mentioned on menus, or 'accidentally' adding extra items to the bill.
scams.avoidance: Always request 'une carafe d'eau' for free tap water. Check menu prices before ordering. Review your bill carefully before paying. Know that service is included - additional tipping is optional.
scams.location: Tourist restaurants near Place de la Comedie, Rue de l'Ancien Courrier, terrace restaurants in Ecusson

scams.name: Les Halles Castellane Market Pickpocketing
scams.description: Montpellier's popular markets draw crowds and pickpockets alike. The bustling atmosphere, narrow aisles between stalls, and shoppers focused on produce create ideal conditions for theft. Pickpockets work alone or in teams, using the crowd and natural jostling as cover.
scams.avoidance: Wear bags closed and in front of your body. Don't put phones or wallets in back pockets. Be extra alert when examining goods at stalls. Keep shopping bags closed and close to your body.
scams.location: Les Halles Castellane, Plan Cabanes market, Marche du Lez, street markets

scams.name: Rental Car Break-In
scams.description: Southern France has high rates of car break-ins, and rental cars are prime targets. Thieves identify rentals by company stickers, foreign plates, or luggage visible inside. They stake out tourist sites, knowing how long visitors typically stay, then break windows to steal bags and valuables. Rest stops along the A9 motorway are particularly notorious.
scams.avoidance: Never leave any belongings visible in the car - even empty bags look promising. Store items in the trunk before arriving at destinations. Remove or cover rental company stickers. Use attended underground parking.
scams.location: Tourist attraction parking areas, beach parking at Palavas and Carnon, A9 motorway rest stops

scams.name: ATM Skimming
scams.description: Criminals install skimming devices on ATMs that capture your card data and PIN. These devices are designed to look like part of the machine and are difficult to detect. Tourist areas are targeted because they process many foreign cards and victims are less familiar with how local ATMs should look.
scams.avoidance: Use ATMs inside bank branches during business hours. Wiggle the card slot and keypad before inserting your card. Cover the keypad with your hand when entering your PIN. Monitor your account for unauthorized transactions.
scams.location: ATMs in tourist areas, street-facing ATMs near Place de la Comedie, train station ATMs

scams.name: Distraction Theft / Bump and Lift
scams.description: Thieves work in teams using distraction techniques. One person creates a diversion - dropping something, asking for directions, bumping into you 'accidentally,' or causing a commotion - while an accomplice steals your valuables. The bump happens so naturally that victims don't realize they've been robbed until the thieves have vanished.
scams.avoidance: Keep moving if someone tries to stop you unnecessarily. If someone bumps you, immediately check your valuables. Don't get drawn into distractions. Wear bags across your body with zippers facing inward.
scams.location: Busy pedestrian streets in the Ecusson, Esplanade de l'Europe, tram boarding areas

scams.name: Nighttime Saint-Roch Area Crime
scams.description: The area between Montpellier's historic Ecusson district and the Saint-Roch train station has a bad reputation at night. After nightlife crowds disperse (especially after 2 AM), opportunistic crime increases in the quieter streets. Tourists walking back to hotels near the station face elevated risk of confrontation or robbery.
scams.avoidance: Take taxis or ride-sharing after late nights out. Stick to well-lit, busy main streets. Don't walk alone late at night. Stay in central, well-connected neighborhoods.
scams.location: Streets between Ecusson and Gare Saint-Roch, around the train station after dark
